name: Steam railway traction
summary: In 1804 a steam locomotive hauled a loaded train along the Merthyr Tramroad in Wales, showing that steam engines could pull loads on rails.
description: A steam locomotive hauled a loaded train on the Merthyr Tramroad in 1804, establishing a working steam railway-traction configuration.
tier_reason: Steam traction supports subsequent railway transport and industrial logistics over generations; the reconstructed exhibit is not the innovation.
why: Ironworks around Merthyr Tydfil moved heavy iron along horse-drawn tramroads, and a high-pressure engine was light enough to move itself.

date.basis: The named source records this distinct community episode; public accounts provide awareness rather than acceptance.
